page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this server provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at 2.8 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core and memory capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in memory bandwidth tests, specifically for uncached large-block read and write operations, as well as in PassMark memory scores. Multi-threaded workloads, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks falling into the average range.

A notable performance tradeoff is observed in low-parameter language model inference; text generation for a small 135M model ranks in the bottom tier, whereas text generation for larger 7B and 70B models achieves strong performance. Given the high network throughput, top-tier database operation benchmarks, and strong multi-core scaling, this instance is suited for network-intensive applications, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation. The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation provide predictable resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads.
